  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",

  "task_id": "LEV-CH01-ONE-STEP-GENERAL-CURRENT-DATA-PRODUCTION-20260908",
  "source_sha256": "b3adec0d3616dbde57a5522cfce1861890887d7c03a2232d2136cb94c9bac1d5",
  "dossier_sha256": "49af125e6e9e6f448a7e92c12a9db69977e76d237b0de2f8acff2af2ac3ebaa6",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "Eq",
      "reuse_sha256": "63522a7f14c7909bdc3b74e40f3dff8106b1aeec727b838bb5857305fb16dbba",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses identical current data, identical next outputs, and equality of the advance function with its factorization.",
      "source_match": "Exact equality expresses determination: fixing current data fixes the next numerical solution. Function equality states this for every modeled history.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "Exists",
      "reuse_sha256": "b8e037b7ee8454967abd5ede341767dc41b18fd412a2ea7e9d3856f010a1dd5f",
      "effect_on_target": "Quantifies a step function on attainable current data, separately for each choice of current and advance.",
      "source_match": "Represents determination by current data without requiring a specified formula or an update on unattainable inputs.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "Function.comp",
      "interpretation": "The supplied body maps f, g, and x to f (g x).",
      "effect_on_target": "The factored advance first extracts the current data with its range-membership certificate and then applies step.",
      "source_match": "The next output receives information from the history through current data alone, matching the selected dependence claim.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "Iff",
      "reuse_sha256": "385655c0e31bfe0bd19fe9a99c72f90b960c605078ce507320f666f7270060f6",
      "effect_on_target": "Equates constancy of advance on equal-current-data histories with factorization through attainable current data.",
      "source_match": "These are equivalent mathematical readings of determination by current data. The equivalence does not assert that an arbitrary advance is one-step.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "Set.Elem",
      "interpretation": "The supplied body constructs the subtype of values satisfying membership in the given set.",
      "effect_on_target": "Restricts the argument of step to current-data values that occur for some history.",
      "source_match": "The source does not demand a total update on an arbitrary ambient data space. Membership certificates do not supply distinct history information: they are proofs of a proposition.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "Set.range",
      "interpretation": "The supplied body defines the set of x for which some input y satisfies f y = x.",
      "effect_on_target": "The update domain contains exactly the values current history for modeled histories.",
      "source_match": "This preserves all data represented by the modeled process and avoids an unsupported extension to unattainable data.",
      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "Set.rangeFactorization",
      "interpretation": "The supplied body sends i to the subtype value whose underlying value is f i and whose certificate proves membership in the range.",
      "effect_on_target": "Feeds step the actual current data of each history. Its proof component certifies attainability without selecting an additional historical input.",
      "source_match": "Preserves the current-data object and the direction from current data to next output.",
      "status": "pass"
    }
  ],
  "semantic_checklist": [
    {
      "id": "C01",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Attached raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, Section 1.7, second paragraph introduces Q, its spatial and temporal indices, and the one-step dependence sentence. Page 33 continues with vector-component conventions; page 31 supplies preceding reference-section context.",
      "lean_evidence": "The proof-free header and both elaborated types present the same equivalence between current-data determination and attainable-domain factorization.",
      "reasoning": "The selected result is the one-step characterization within explanatory notation prose. The adjacent notation conventions clarify its interpretation. Source identity and hashes are supplied provenance, not independently recomputed here."
    },
    {
      "id": "C02",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Page 32 leaves the contents of current-time data unspecified and identifies the resulting solution as numerical through the surrounding Q paragraph.",
      "lean_evidence": "History and NextData are arbitrary sorts; CurrentData is an arbitrary type; current and advance share the History domain.",
      "reasoning": "History can represent admissible executions or contexts at a fixed transition, current extracts their current-time data, and advance gives their next numerical solution. No scalar, stencil, or dimensional restriction is imposed."
    },
    {
      "id": "C03",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The next numerical solution is determined entirely by current-time data for the one-step methods under discussion.",
      "lean_evidence": "For each current and advance, all pairs of histories are compared; the existential step is outside the history comparisons and satisfies a function equality.",
      "reasoning": "One step function serves all histories for the chosen process. It may depend on the selected process and fixed transition; the theorem does not require a single map shared by different times or methods."
    },
    {
      "id": "C04",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The passage concerns one-step methods and gives no stability, positivity, regularity, or ambient-domain admissibility assumptions.",
      "lean_evidence": "The left side is the equal-current-data determination property. No numerical side conditions are added, and step is defined on Set.range current.",
      "reasoning": "The left side formalizes the relevant one-step condition rather than assuming every process has it. Admissible histories can be represented by History without requiring an extension to inadmissible data."
    },
    {
      "id": "C05",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The selected anchor is the dependence of the solution at t_{n+1} on data at t_n. The neighboring sentences explain suppression of temporal superscripts.",
      "lean_evidence": "The left side expresses determination, and the right side expresses a function of current data producing every advance output.",
      "reasoning": "The entire selected dependence characterization is represented. The surrounding conventions about omitted superscripts and the book's choice of methods are contextual prose, not additional mathematical conclusions of this selected result."
    },
    {
      "id": "C06",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The passage supplies a verbal dependence claim without a numerical update formula.",
      "lean_evidence": "D001-D007 consist of equality, existence, equivalence, composition, the range subtype, its defining existential membership, and its canonical factorization.",
      "reasoning": "Each dependency has been interpreted from its supplied body or exact validated meaning reuse. Together they express functional dependence without introducing a numerical operator."
    },
    {
      "id": "C07",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Entire determination by current data requires the same next solution whenever that data is the same.",
      "lean_evidence": "current history₁ = current history₂ implies advance history₁ = advance history₂, equivalently advance = step composed with rangeFactorization current.",
      "reasoning": "Equality has the appropriate strength. The reverse direction of the equivalence is a definitional consequence of dependence through a function, not an extra numerical assertion."
    },
    {
      "id": "C08",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Page 32 distinguishes q, its numerical approximation Q, and the more general current-time data.",
      "lean_evidence": "CurrentData and NextData are separate parameters, and current and advance have distinct roles.",
      "reasoning": "The formalization does not identify current data exclusively with Q or equate the next numerical output with the exact PDE solution. History provides the domain over which dependence is tested."
    },
    {
      "id": "C09",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The stated transition is from t_n to t_{n+1}; no step size or time-independent update is specified.",
      "lean_evidence": "current and advance encode the input and output of a selected transition. No time index, coefficient, or step-size constant occurs.",
      "reasoning": "Abstracting a fixed transition preserves the current-to-next relation. Separate instantiations may represent different n, so the existential step imposes no autonomy across time."
    },
    {
      "id": "C10",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Pages 32-33 permit different spatial indexing and vector-valued systems, while leaving current data unspecified.",
      "lean_evidence": "All three object domains are generic; the update domain is the exact range of current.",
      "reasoning": "The type abstraction covers these source cases. Restriction to the range excludes no modeled history and avoids asserting totality beyond the modeled data. The generic formulation is a logical abstraction of the selected dependence property."
    },
    {
      "id": "C11",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The source gives no rule for unattainable current data or degenerate abstract domains.",
      "lean_evidence": "Set.range current admits exactly attained values; History is not assumed inhabited.",
      "reasoning": "No undefined application is required. Empty-history instances yield an empty update domain, while all nonempty intended instances remain covered. If History is inhabited, the supplied advance already entails available NextData values."
    },
    {
      "id": "C12",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The one-step sentence describes a substantive restriction on temporal dependence.",
      "lean_evidence": "The equal-current-data condition is an operand of Iff, not an unconditional assertion about advance.",
      "reasoning": "Nontrivial satisfying instances exist: histories (x, p), current (x, p) = x, and advance (x, p) = x + 1 over natural numbers. With advance (x, p) = p instead, equal current data can give different outputs, and neither side holds. Thus the characterization distinguishes dependence from history dependence and does not rely on empty domains."
    },
    {
      "id": "N01",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The passage characterizes one-step methods without specifying a particular discretization or recurrence.",
      "lean_evidence": "advance is the modeled next output, and the factorization asserts that its dependence on a history passes through current.",
      "reasoning": "This is the execution-dependence property selected from the source. Since no concrete numerical scheme is selected, no further formula linkage is required."
    },
    {
      "id": "N02",
      "status": "not-applicable",
      "source_evidence": "The selected sentence contains no norm or metric. Adjacent vector notation does not impose a componentwise numerical relation here.",
      "lean_evidence": "The target uses equality of generic objects, without a norm, metric, or component operator.",
      "reasoning": "There is no norm or component convention to compare in this dependence characterization."
    },
    {
      "id": "N03",
      "status": "not-applicable",
      "source_evidence": "The selected passage makes no error, conditioning, or stability claim.",
      "lean_evidence": "No error or stability predicate appears.",
      "reasoning": "The proposition concerns information dependence only."
    },
    {
      "id": "N04",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "The enclosing paragraph identifies Q as a numerical approximation to q before discussing the next-time solution.",
      "lean_evidence": "advance returns a NextData object; the theorem asserts only equality between such outputs and their factored representation.",
      "reasoning": "Interpreting NextData as numerical solution data preserves the source role. Exact equality here concerns identical computed outputs for identical inputs, not exact agreement with q."
    },
    {
      "id": "N05",
      "status": "not-applicable",
      "source_evidence": "No limiting process, asymptotic estimate, or omitted higher-order term occurs in the selected passage.",
      "lean_evidence": "The target is an exact logical equivalence without asymptotic operators.",
      "reasoning": "There is no asymptotic status to preserve."
    },
    {
      "id": "N06",
      "status": "pass",
      "source_evidence": "Determination by current data entails a unique next output for that data, but the source specifies no update on arbitrary unattainable values.",
      "lean_evidence": "advance supplies outputs for modeled histories; the left side enforces agreement on each current-data fiber, and step is required only on that range.",
      "reasoning": "A representative history supplies existence for each attained datum, while fiber constancy makes its output independent of the representative. Conversely a step function ensures that agreement. No PDE well-posedness or computable construction is asserted."
    }
  ],
  "implications": {
    "lean_implies_source": {
      "verdict": "yes",
      "reasoning": "Under the selected source context, interpret History as admissible histories for a fixed method and transition, current as their data at t_n, and advance as their numerical solution at t_{n+1}. The equivalence identifies independence from histories sharing current data with an update using only attainable current data. This is the selected verbal characterization of one-step dependence; it does not claim every advance has that property."
    },
    "source_implies_lean": {
      "verdict": "yes",
      "reasoning": "The source's determination condition means that histories with identical current data have identical next outputs. On each attained datum, choosing a history produces a well-defined output because of that condition, giving the factored step map. Conversely, a factored map necessarily gives equal outputs on equal current data. This is the classical functional reformulation of the selected characterization, without additional totality or time-independence requirements."
    }
  },
  "classification": "faithful-equivalent",
  "accepted": true,
  "requires_adjudication": false,
  "findings": [],
  "rationale": "The attached authoritative page images support a general characterization of one-step dependence, not a specific numerical formula. The target represents that characterization by the equivalence between fiber constancy and factorization through attained current data. Its abstract domains preserve general current data, and a fixed-transition interpretation permits explicit time and method dependence across instantiations. It asserts neither that arbitrary methods are one-step nor that updates extend to unattainable inputs. All supplied dependencies and configured checks are resolved. The supplied hashes identify the evidence; they were not independently recomputed."
}
